title: Real-client blend bench journal — Kai
content:
Purpose:
Capture a compact, reproducible lab log where we replay a blended set of real client traces (three customers) against private-stage to validate tail behavior with mixed small/long responses and intermittent bursts. Goal is fast triage for whether the p99+ tail is client payload or scheduler/backpressure related.

Environment snapshot:
- cluster: private-stage (8 x A10G), service build: inference-2025.01.27
- runtime flags: --continuous-batching --kv-cache-enabled --idle-eviction-ms=1200
- model: llama2-13b-q4f16 (quantized shim), sequence cap 1024, tokenizer: byte-level
- bench tool: bench-runner:v0.7.3 (local), replay harness uses blended trace mixer (see linked PR)

Trace composition (blended):
- Customer A (mobile-chat): 65% of requests, avg tokens 42, 95th tokens 120 (short/medium)
- Customer B (assist-long): 25% of requests, avg tokens 520, 95th tokens 800 (long responses)
- Customer C (burst-probe): 10% of requests, very spiky with rapid bursts (microbursts ~ 1–2s windows)
- Arrival pattern: base Poisson (lambda = 35 r/s) + superposed bursts drawn from recorded timestamps (preserves cluster autocorrelation)

Experiment matrix (runs):
1) Baseline — no burst injection, concurrency cap 64, batching=auto
2) Burst-only — injected recorded Customer C bursts, concurrency cap 128, batching=auto
3) Long-heavy — boost Customer B weight to 45%, concurrency cap 64, batching=auto
4) Throttle test — concurrency cap 32, inject burst, batching=auto
5) Batch-off — same as Baseline but batching disabled on runtime

Key commands (local):
- bench-runner replay --trace blend.yaml --duration 1800 --target-host private-stage:443 --concurrency 64 --out results/baseline.csv
- bench-runner profile --heatmap results/baseline.csv --bucket 10ms --out charts/baseline-heatmap.png

Selected results (aggregated, median of 3 runs each):
- Baseline: mean RPS 32.6, p50 57ms, p95 182ms, p99 412ms, p999 1.32s, error rate 0.12%
- Burst-only: mean RPS 38.9 (burst spikes up to 210 r/s), p50 61ms, p95 255ms, p99 1.12s, p999 3.6s, error rate 0.9%
- Long-heavy: mean RPS 27.2, p50 88ms, p95 420ms, p99 1.9s, p999 4.2s, error rate 0.7%
- Throttle test: mean RPS 24.1, p50 95ms, p95 510ms, p99 2.6s, p999 6.5s, error rate 3.1%
- Batch-off: mean RPS 21.5, p50 110ms, p95 620ms, p99 3.9s, p999 9.1s, error rate 4.8%

Quick observations / hypotheses:
- Batching provides substantial headroom for short responses (Baseline vs Batch-off: ~50% higher RPS).
- Under burst conditions p999 grows nonlinearly; suspect queueing + preemption of long requests causing head-of-line effects.
- Long-heavy mixes drive up p99 significantly even with modest overall RPS — KV cache hits drop due to longer generation windows.
- Throttling (low concurrency cap) increases error rate and p999 a lot — suggests backpressure and retry cascades rather than graceful queueing.

Tiny ascii heatmap (bi-modal tail hint) — p99 timeline for Burst-only run (seconds):
[0s] =======---===-----======---=====---====  (1.12s)
[30s] =======----===------========-----===== (1.02s)
[60s] =========----==-------=======-----===== (1.34s)
(visual only, actual heatmaps saved to charts/)

Immediate next steps (short):
- Re-run Burst-only with --idle-eviction-ms=600 and observe p999. Hypothesis: faster eviction reduces head-of-line by freeing slots.
- Add measurements split by request size (bin small/med/long) to see per-class tail. bench-runner already supports --group-by=size-bin
- Capture runtime thread/queue depth telemetry during Throttle test (SRE hooks) to distinguish reject vs queue-timeouts

Follow-ups (medium):
- Try policy: "prefer-short-first" scheduling (simulate by shuffling long requests lower priority) to estimate latency gains for short queries.
- Experiment quantization variant q3a vs q4f16 to see cost/latency tradeoff for long responses (long-heavy test)

Notes to self:
- Save raw traces + seed for blender. Currently at experiments/traces/blend-seed-20250218.tgz
- Push a minimal reproducible cond to the PR linked above so Lina can run locally
- Marcus: ask SRE to temporarily enable extra tracing on private-stage when we re-run (low-overhead sample at 1%)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are some p999 spikes correlated to GC/driver stalls on A10s? Need NVML timeline aligned with bench-runner timestamps.
- When batching is off p95->p999 degradation is huge. Is there a single component (scheduler vs kernel launch) responsible?

Conclusion (draft):
Batching + prioritizing short responses looks like the fastest win for user-visible latency at 90–95th percentiles. The high end tail (p999) is a combination of burst arrival patterns and long-response interference — we need targeted experiments that separate queueing/backpressure from kernel/driver stalls.

TODO (short):

- [ ] Draft short notes for product on tradeoffs (1 page)

End of entry.
